subtitle: 10 questions on this week's words, in real GMAT format. Older words from 3–4 weeks ago come back too.
instructions: You have 120 seconds per question; the quiz moves on when time runs out.
Your score appears the moment you finish.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
The board of a major Indian retail conglomerate recently proposed a plan to aggressively expand physical storefronts in Tier-3 cities. However, market analysts argue that the strategy is misguided because rural consumer demand remains unpredictable and fragmented. The analysts suggest that management should instead acquiesce to investor demands for digital-first infrastructure. 

Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the market analysts' argument?
options: Tier-3 city consumers have consistently shown a preference for in-person product verification before making high-value purchases.
Management has already allocated a significant portion of next year's budget to software development.
Investors are generally unwilling to support long-term capital expenditure plans without immediate returns.
Competitors in Tier-1 cities are experiencing declining profit margins due to high operational costs.
Digital infrastructure in rural areas has improved slightly over the past two fiscal quarters.
questions.explanation: The target word 'acquiesce' means to accept or agree passively. The analysts argue management should yield (acquiesce) to investor demand for digital expansion because rural physical demand is unpredictable; option A directly undermines this by showing strong local consumer demand for physical stores, justifying the physical expansion over yielding to digital-first demands. Option C is a trap because while it discusses investor mindset, it does not address the core issue of consumer purchasing behavior in Tier-3 cities.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
During the recent regulatory audit, financial consultants discovered several aberrant trading transactions executed by the firm's algorithmic desk during off-peak hours. The head of trading claimed these outliers were merely benign technical glitches caused by a temporary server migration. Consequently, the executive committee decided not to launch a full forensic investigation.

Which of the following highlights a flaw in the executive committee's reasoning?
options: It assumes that server migrations never cause minor execution delays in automated trading systems.
It takes for granted that abnormal transaction patterns can be dismissed without verifying whether they masked unauthorized activity.
It fails to consider that the financial consultants were hired specifically to identify software bugs.
It ignores the possibility that competitors were also experiencing similar algorithmic anomalies.
It relies on evidence gathered only after the trading desk had already corrected the technical glitch.
questions.explanation: The argument describes 'aberrant' (deviating from the norm/abnormal) trades and flaws the decision to accept a simple explanation without investigation. Option B correctly identifies the logical flaw: uncritically accepting that abnormal patterns were harmless without verification. Option A is a trap that reverses the assumption of the trading head rather than pointing out the committee's logical leap.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
A prominent tech start-up in Bengaluru published an abstruse white paper detailing its new proprietary encryption protocol. The executive team asserted that because no rival firm has publicly critiqued or replicated the underlying mathematical proof, the protocol is mathematically unhackable.

Which of the following is an assumption required by the executive team's argument?
options: Rival firms possess both the expertise to comprehend the complex proof and an interest in publicly challenging it.
The proprietary protocol will become the industry standard for cybersecurity within the next decade.
Engineers who authored the white paper used standard academic notation to present their findings.
No external cybersecurity firm was compensated to conduct an independent audit of the protocol.
Rival firms have attempted to build competing protocols using alternative encryption methods.
questions.explanation: The paper is described as 'abstruse' (obscure and difficult to understand). The author assumes that silence from rivals implies the proof is solid; option A explicitly states the necessary assumption that rivals actually understood the obscure paper and cared to challenge it. Option C is a trap because standard notation does not guarantee rivals reviewed or tried to replicate it.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
When the government announced a new green-energy subsidy, the logistics company responded with remarkable alacrity, applying for grants and ordering electric delivery fleets within forty-eight hours. Industry observers concluded that the company's rapid pivot proves it prioritized environmental sustainability above short-term profitability.

Which of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the observers' conclusion?
options: The subsidy fully covered the purchase price of the electric vehicles while significantly reducing operational fuel overhead.
The company had previously fallen behind its primary competitors in adopting digital tracking tools.
Several smaller delivery firms applied for the same government subsidies a week after the initial announcement.
The government required all subsidy recipients to submit quarterly emissions reports for five years.
The company's board of directors had been considering fleet upgrades for over two years.
questions.explanation: Alacrity' means eager and prompt readiness. Observers attribute this fast reaction to a selfless eco-friendly mission, but option A provides an alternative, profit-driven explanation (full coverage of cost plus lower overhead) that undermines the claim that sustainability was prioritized *over* profit. Option E explains prior planning, but does not weaken the claim regarding financial motive as strongly as A.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
A fintech startup found that traditional small-business owners in semi-urban India are rarely amenable to adopting automated digital accounting applications. To increase adoption, the company plans to introduce human assistance agents who will personally guide business owners through the software onboarding process.

Which of the following, if true, provides the strongest support for the startup's plan?
options: Small-business owners who receive personalized, in-person demonstrations are far more receptive to shifting from paper ledgers to software.
Traditional small businesses currently pay higher tax penalties due to errors in manual bookkeeping.
Automated digital accounting tools are significantly cheaper than hiring full-time accountants.
Competitors offering similar applications rely entirely on automated chat support for customer onboarding.
The cost of hiring human assistance agents will decrease as the startup expands its geographic reach.
questions.explanation: The prompt notes that business owners are not 'amenable' (open, receptive, or agreeable) to digital accounting software. Option A directly strengthens the plan by showing that human assistance overcomes this lack of open receptivity. Option B shows a problem with bookkeeping, but doesn't prove human agents will make owners receptive to software.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
The CEO of an emerging pharmaceutical firm proposed an audacious strategy: double the annual R&D expenditure to develop novel gene therapies, despite the company having only six months of cash reserves remaining. The CEO claims this move will secure market dominance before legacy competitors can react.

Which of the following, if true, highlights the greatest risk in the CEO's proposed strategy?
options: Legacy competitors have already established long-standing distribution contracts with domestic hospital networks.
Developing novel gene therapies typically requires several years of clinical trials before regulatory approval and revenue generation.
The firm's existing product line currently generates steady, albeit modest, positive cash flows.
R&D spending in the pharmaceutical industry has grown at an average rate of eight percent annually across the region.
Scientific researchers in the biotechnology sector command higher salaries than software engineers.
questions.explanation: An 'audacious' plan is exceptionally bold or daring, often carrying high risk. The CEO's bold plan risks immediate insolvency because cash reserves last only 6 months; option B points out that clinical trials take years, ensuring the company will run out of cash long before seeing revenue. Option A is a market hurdle, but B exposes the fatal flaw in the financial timeline.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
Following intense pushback from small merchants regarding high transaction surcharges, the municipal transport authority decided to rescind its policy mandating exclusive cashless payments for public transit passes. The authority announced that cash would once again be accepted at all ticketing kiosks starting next month.

If the statement above is true, which of the following must also be true?
options: Public transit ridership will return to peak levels recorded prior to the cashless mandate.
The authority's original mandate for exclusive cashless payments will no longer remain in effect starting next month.
Small merchants will see an immediate increase in daily retail revenue due to transit passengers.
Cashless payment technologies are inefficient for high-volume municipal transit systems.
The transport authority will reduce ticket prices to compensate merchants for past losses.
questions.explanation: To 'rescind' means to revoke, cancel, or repeal a law or policy. If the authority rescinds the mandate and accepts cash next month, then by definition the exclusive cashless mandate will no longer be in effect (Option B). Option A makes an unwarranted projection about ridership numbers.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
The lead researcher publicly repudiated the findings of the university's landmark agronomy study, declaring that the data collected from trial farms had been systematically altered by an external commercial sponsor. The university administration responded by forming an independent ethics panel to evaluate the study's integrity.

Which of the following statements is best supported by the information above?
options: The university administration had prior knowledge of the commercial sponsor's data manipulation.
The trial farm results cannot be considered reliable evidence without further independent verification.
The lead researcher resigned from the university prior to publicizing the statement.
Commercial sponsors are prohibited from funding academic agronomy research at the university.
The independent ethics panel will recommend the complete withdrawal of all published papers.
questions.explanation: To 'repudiate' means to disown, reject, or deny the validity of something. Since the lead researcher publicly rejected the study's findings due to altered data, it logically follows that the trial farm results cannot be relied upon without verification (Option B). Option E assumes the panel's conclusion, which is not stated.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
An internal audit of a state-owned infrastructure enterprise revealed an egregious accounting oversight: over 400 crore rupees in supplier liabilities had been omitted from balance sheets for three consecutive fiscal years. Senior managers argued that the omission was a harmless clerical mistake caused by transitioning to a new enterprise resource planning software.

Which of the following, if true, most strongly refutes the senior managers' defense?
options: The omitted liabilities conveniently allowed the enterprise to meet executive bonus targets linked to artificial profitability metrics.
The software transition was completed six months later than originally scheduled by the IT department.
Several lower-level accountants had received training on the new enterprise software prior to its rollout.
Other state-owned enterprises in the sector reported minor accounting discrepancies during software upgrades.
The enterprise hired an external consulting firm to assist with financial reporting in the subsequent year.
questions.explanation: Egregious' means extraordinarily bad or flagrant. The management claims an extraordinary error was just a harmless software mistake; option A refutes this by showing a clear financial incentive (executive bonuses tied to artificial profit), pointing to intentional fraud rather than a harmless glitch. Option C shows training occurred, but doesn't prove motive as directly as A.

questions.label: Critical Reasoning
questions.prompt:
A venture capital fund partner conducted a cursory review of an AI startup's pitch deck during a taxi ride and immediately decided to invest two million dollars. The partner reasoned that because the founders graduated from a top engineering institute, the underlying tech architecture must be sound.

Which of the following describes a flaw in the partner's decision-making process?
options: It bases a major financial investment on a brief, superficial evaluation rather than rigorous due diligence.
It assumes that top engineering institutes only offer degrees in artificial intelligence and computer science.
It relies on historical investment returns from unrelated industries to project future tech valuations.
It underestimates the time required for early-stage startups to achieve sustainable profitability.
It fails to consider whether competing venture capital funds were also evaluating the startup.
questions.explanation: Cursory' means hasty and detailed-lacking (superficial). Option A correctly identifies the flaw: relying on a brief, superficial (cursory) glance and founder credentials instead of conducting proper diligence. Option B overstates what the partner assumed about degree offerings.
